thread:
incident-bot: Pager: elevated 5xx + tail latency for hosted-inference in az1a. Impact: ~18% errors on generation endpoints. Auto-fanout triggered to eu1a. Paging oncall-sre.
oncall-sre: on it. seeing spike in NLB 502/504s from backend g5 nodes.
eng-runtime-amy: logs show repeated `write: broken pipe` from worker processes, kernel tx queue growing on eth0.
infra-josh: on the host side I can see `qdisc pfifo_fast` backlog. running `tc -s qdisc show dev eth0` now.
network-lee: any DNS signs? resolver latency in az1a recently high. If backend nodes not reachable, NLB will 502.
eng-runtime-amy: DNS looks ok for control plane. This is local transmit stall. I can repro with `iperf` to neighbor instance — tx stalls after sustained bursts.
oncall-sre: are we seeing recent kernel updates or instance type changes?
infra-josh: no kernel ops in the last 24h. We did roll some capacity in the node pool ~3h ago (scale up ephemeral g5).
eng-oncall: suggestion: temporarily divert traffic from this AZ for the model pools with high qps. Add an az routing rule with weight=0 for az1a.
pm-sara: customer-ops, heads-up: a handful of customers on high-throughput plans might see failed requests. We should prepare status.
customer-ops: yes please. severity? ETA for mitigation?
oncall-sre: mitigation plan: 1) mark az1a nodes as draining for inference-route 2) scale up eu1a dedicated pool 3) run health-check tweaks to avoid sticky connections 4) follow up root cause.
eng-runtime-amy: executing `kubectl label nodes az=az1a-inference drain=true` for route-config to prefer other zones.
infra-josh: starting a rolling infra-level cordon on the impacted kube nodes and restarting nic drivers on a small subset (1 node) to test.
network-lee: I can also add a resolver fallback policy for local DNS TTLs so control-plane lookups don't hang.
eng-oncall: traffic reroute now applied, testing. hitting same model endpoints from us-west and getting normal p95.
oncall-sre: metrics show error rate dropping to 3% after reroute. Nice.
eng-runtime-amy: quick workaround: reduce keepalive on worker pool and enable connection retry with short backoff to avoid stuck sockets. Pushing config change.`service/runtime: set KEEPALIVE_MS=5000, RETRY_BACKOFF_MS=150`
pm-sara: drafting status update for customers: brief note about an AZ transmit issue, mitigation applied, monitoring.
customer-ops: send initial note: "We're seeing higher errors in one AZ, traffic is being rerouted, no data loss, mitigation in progress."
oncall-sre: infra-josh — what's the outcome of the driver restart on the test node?
infra-josh: driver restart freed the tx queue, that node recovered. But other nodes show intermittent recurrence. Looks like a transient qdisc/tc bug on this instance type under sustained gso/gro traffic patterns.
network-lee: filing an AWS support ticket referencing potential NIC offload path degradation. Will request deeper NIC telemetry.
eng-runtime-amy: we should avoid wide-scale restarts. prefer routing + gradual node replacement.
oncall-sre: agreed. keeping az1a weight=0 for now. Monitoring for 30m then plan for controlled repro and RCA.
eng-oncall: adding a canary to bring one model pool back into az1a with slower qps to validate.
pm-sara: customer update posted to status.redwood.ai: "We've routed traffic away from the affected AZ, customers may see transient errors. Working on remediation; we'll follow up."
customer-ops: queued a handful of proactive emails for top customers.
eng-runtime-amy: capturing kdump and tx stats for the nodes we drained. saving artifacts to /var/log/incident/1745009876/
oncall-sre: good. leaving this thread on watch. if any regression ping @oncall-sre. :eyes:
incident-bot: Incident tagged P2; note created in pager duty."
